clue.text: Cancel call before start

indicators.note: the call word is placed ahead of the start word in the answer

parts.note: to call out is to cry
the off is the start of a race, as in 'from the off'

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon a phone call before it begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out of an arrangement is to withdraw from it, a phrasal synonym for calling it off.

clue.text: Try again-it turns out to be correct

explanation.surface: A retest proves that a claim was right after all.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove something a second time is to test it anew, and to reprimand or rebuke someone is to correct them.

clue.text: Jolly Roger, endless focus of fear

indicators.note: jolly signals a merry jumbling of the letters
the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The pirate flag, ever the centre of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ROGER to ROGE, and 'Jolly' rearranges it. The Jolly Roger is the pirate skull-and-crossbones flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale monster is a frightening figure, the object of terror.

clue.text: Fail completely as key total's down

parts.note: F is a musical key
the total is all of something
flat means down or dejected

explanation.surface: A complete failure because the important sum has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or plan that falls flat flops entirely, to the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Rings about royal items of jewellery

indicators.note: the bell word goes round the royal letter, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: rings of bells are peals
R is the usual abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Bands surrounding regal jewels, as in a crown collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous gems formed in oysters are worn as necklace stones, so they are jewellery items.

clue.text: Considerable fine

explanation.surface: A large penalty imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sizeable amount is 'a pretty penny', and attractive or good-looking means fine.

clue.text: Article in case-it turned out to be Monday of pleasing appearance

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Article in case-it turned out to be Monday of pleasing appearance' (9): AESTHETIC is A + an anagram of CASE IT plus THE, but no THE is in the held clue; 'to be Monday' looks garbled by OCR and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Article in case-it turned out to be Monday of pleasing appearance

clue.text: Run after the French composer's pupil

indicators.note: the run letter is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: le is French for the
Thomas Arne was an English composer of Rule, Britannia!
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A student of a French composer following in his footsteps.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who is still being taught a skill, such as a novice driver.

clue.text: Indissoluble bond?

parts.note: reads like an unbreakable marriage or friendship, but describes a very strong adhesive that sticks things for good

explanation.definitionFit: A cyanoacrylate glue sets so firmly that the join cannot be dissolved, an unbreakable bond.

clue.text: Insufficient trade to cheat one's customers?

parts.note: short means lacking enough
to change one thing for another is to trade it

explanation.surface: Poor dealing amounts to swindling the shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give too little money back to a buyer is to defraud them.

clue.text: Note that's pointed

explanation.surface: A remark described as barbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note raised a semitone has this name, and a blade with a fine tip is keen-edged too.

clue.text: Affected pet's routine badly

indicators.note: the words are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A pet's daily habits poorly performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PETS ROUTINE, using the S of pet's.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and putting on airs is the same as being mannered or affected.

clue.text: Get round in order to see music producer

indicators.note: the round letter is placed inside the order, signalled by this word

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to get a circle of people organised before a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour; O sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument produces music, so the double-reed pipe is called a music producer here.

clue.text: Not much hope American can fetch a replacement

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are put in a new arrangement, replaced in order

explanation.surface: A gloomy view that a US tin can bring along a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a tin in the surface; it is fodder, and 'replacement' is the signal to rearrange the three words that follow American.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic idiom means there is almost no likelihood of something happening.

clue.text: Specific hype about a performer

parts.note: the definite article 'the' marks something specific

indicators.note: the hype word goes round the letter A here

parts.note: spin is media hype or slanted promotion

explanation.surface: A precise bit of publicity concerning a stage artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' giving the definite article is a crossword convention; 'about' wraps the hype word round A.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is called this, after Thespis, the legendary first Greek dramatist.

clue.text: Team's ready for TV show

parts.note: a panel is a team of people, as on a quiz
game means willing or ready, as in 'I'm game'

explanation.surface: A side prepared to go on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast quiz where celebrities on a team answer questions is a television programme.

clue.text: Short, as rent's reduced by a quarter

indicators.note: the tears word is made smaller by losing the letter A

parts.note: rents in cloth are tears, so the plural gives tears
E, for east, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A complaint that a landlord's rent has been cut by a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent's' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the plural of a rip; 'reduced by' removes A, and 'a quarter' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief and curt speech is clipped, abrupt in few words.

clue.text: Decided to get in drink for regular

indicators.note: the decided word is put inside the drink

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink of fermented honey
sure means certain, decided

explanation.surface: A resolution to buy a round for a familiar pub customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular' looks like a pub regular, which the drink encourages; it is the definition, meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady, even rhythm or pace is called measured, a regular one.

clue.text: Drama about game all around lake

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece is turned round end to end
the drama word goes about the game letters

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A play about a sport, staged in the round by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the game inside the drama, then 'all around' turns everything round end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America, between Michigan and Ontario.

clue.text: Keeps getting nastier, sadly

indicators.note: the word is sadly damaged, so its letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Things grow more unpleasant, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to or preserve something is to keep it.

clue.text: Liking the combination of quiet charm

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to charm someone is to enchant them

explanation.surface: Fondness born of a mix of reserve and allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness or inclination for something is a taste for it.

clue.text: Great to roam round US city for free

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the city
the letters wander off into a new order

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: It would be great to wander freely around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to roam' scrambles the first word so that its letters split around the US city, which 'round' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped criminal on the loose is at liberty, free.

clue.text: Return for match

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
to fit is to match or suit

explanation.surface: Going back to play a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial return on an investment is gain or income.

clue.text: Start Helen's treatment for this medical condition?

indicators.note: the letters of these words are given a new treatment, reworked into another order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A question about beginning a course of medicine for a woman's illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges START HELEN; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria, a stinging skin rash like the reaction to a plant's sting, is a medical complaint.

clue.text: Singer offering piece from Walton

indicators.note: a piece taken from the composer's name, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A vocalist performing a work by the composer William Walton.
explanation.definitionFit: A low female or high male voice, and the vocalist who sings that part.

clue.text: A crop, we're told, that's wrong

indicators.note: signals the words are heard said aloud

parts.note: a crop such as rye, with the article A

explanation.surface: Farmers report that a harvest has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone askew or amiss is going wrong.

clue.text: Girl's caught inside by returning Yorkshire banker

indicators.note: the caught letter is put inside the turned river
the river's name is read backwards, coming back

parts.note: the Aire is a Yorkshire river, and a river has banks, so it is a banker
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl dismissed in cricket by a bank clerk from Yorkshire heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes ERIA of AIRE; C goes inside it. 'banker' is a crossword trick: a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so it fits a clue asking for a girl.

clue.text: Power plant producing brilliant display

parts.note: fire means drive or power, as in firepower
a works is an industrial plant or factory

explanation.surface: An energy station generating a spectacular light show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnics make a dazzling exhibition of light and colour in the night sky.

clue.text: Benefit when securing new agreement

indicators.note: the benefit word holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: an asset is a benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: An advantage gained by locking in a fresh deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent or approval given to a proposal is agreement.

clue.text: Poet's ' dead nice, initially, about Isle of Wight resort

indicators.note: the initials go round the resort, one at each end
the first letters of the two words before it are taken

parts.note: Ryde is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A verse-writer finds a seaside town on the Isle of Wight utterly lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: D and N go about RYDE, a resort on the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the seventeenth-century English Poet Laureate; 'Poet's' is poet is.
